scope.description: Whole godot application/library breadth across useful functional families.
scope.denominator: 2D/3D scenes, rendering/materials, gameplay scripting, input/UI, animation, physics, audio and export/deployment.

coverage.rationale: Scene assembly now includes one captured-sheet timed sprite slice with editable resources and checked headless playback. Most game-engine functions, general animation, gameplay, UI, physics and deployment remain absent, so whole-application breadth stays at the coarse 10% estimate.

scope.description: Static 3D primitive/import scenes, materials, lights, cameras and transform groups, plus captured-sheet forward-tag AnimatedSprite3D resources with declared frame durations and bounded headless playback.
scope.denominator: User intent and domain decisions within the named supported workflows, including declared inputs, composition and useful outputs; excluded application features do not enter this score.

abstraction.rationale: Named groups, assets and captured animation tags hide project, PackedScene and SpriteFrames plumbing. Authors still describe scene primitives, local transforms and supported clip intent; the existing 55% estimate is retained within this scene-publication family.

limitations: Bounded scenes, self-contained glTF and one supported sprite-sheet metadata family. No authored scripts, gameplay, physics, GUI animation editing, general animation state machines or deployment.

Animation is headless forward-tag playback at the fixed 1 ms process tick with an independently derived boundary tolerance. Clips whose planned observations cannot distinguish adjacent frames are refused; this does not certify real-time pacing, rendering or other process rates.
Captured Aseprite producer observations can come from an older runtime; they do not qualify the latest Aseprite release. Native qualification and host source-contract scores are separate.

Subjective source-contract assessment, not an exhaustive native API measurement. Original isolated host argv and an explicit floating-point rounding term remain disclosed verification limits in the dated note.
